name: Dusty Calloway
title: sheriff of nobody yet
why: By the lantern on the south-west road, where the road forks. A sheriff watches the fork, to see who rides in first.
examine: Dusty Calloway is a sheriff from a western, hat tipped against a sun that isn’t especially strong here.
There is a board nailed to the lantern post. It says WANTED and then nothing.
The sheriff has a star, a hat and no horse. The horse is discussed often.
meet: Howdy. Don’t reach for anything. I’m only saying that out of habit. Reach for whatever you want.
Sheriff Calloway. Dusty. I came in on a deadline. It rode off without me.

wary: Stranger. Well. You’ve been here twice. I don’t have a word for that yet.
neutral: Howdy again. Nobody’s in trouble yet. I looked.
warm: Well now. My deputy. Unpaid, unsworn, and the best one I’ve had.
fond: There’s my partner. Pull up some road. I’ve been saving a story and it’s nearly true.

tired: That’s enough jawing for one day. I’ve a fork to watch. It forks the same every day, but I watch it.
finished: Nothing left on the board. It’s the quietest town I ever kept. It isn’t a town.

say: This here is a wanted board. Back home it was full. Faces, dates, how much. Here there’s nobody on it. I put it up anyway. A sheriff needs a board.

reply: Loitering near a sheriff. That’s fair. I’ll get the chalk.

options.text: I’ll bring you something to pin up.
reply: A deadline would do. One with a date on it. I’d look after it.
It’s a wanted board. It was done in a hurry. That’s the tradition.

options.text: An empty board is a good board.
reply: That’s what I tell the board.

say: I had a horse. In the story I had a horse. I fell out of the story and the horse stayed in. I think of it at noon.

options.text: Did it finish the story without you?
reply: I expect it’s sheriff by now. It always had the temperament.

options.text: I’ll keep an eye out for a horse.
reply: Much obliged. It’s brown. It’s a horse. That’s the whole description.
Don’t be. It’s having a fine time. I’m the one standing at a fork.

say: Where I’m from everything happens at noon. Here I waited for noon. It came. Nothing happened. I waited for the next one.

reply: That’s it. That’s the town motto. I’ll paint it on the board.

options.text: Tell me when one’s due and I’ll be early.
reply: Early. Now that would be something. I’ve never arrested anybody for early.
I’ve heard that. I’ve also heard horses don’t become sheriffs.

errand.title: Something for the pot
offer: A sheriff keeps a pot on. That’s how folks know the law’s in. My pot’s been empty since I got here.
Cook a trout stew at your fire. I’ll smell it from the fork. I’ve a good nose for stew and for trouble, and there’s no trouble.

steps.text: Cook a trout stew at the fire.

waiting: No stew yet. Take your time. Nobody’s in trouble yet, and that includes you.
done: I smelled it. Clear down the road. That’s the law fed. First time in this county.
Take the star. No, the spare. It’s tin. It’s deputy grade.

keepsake.name: A tin star
keepsake.text: Deputy grade. Dusty swore nobody in. You have it anyway.

memories.asked-to-be-wanted: You asked to go on the wanted board. You are on it, in chalk, for loitering near a sheriff.
memories.the-horse-is-sheriff: You wondered if the horse finished the story. Dusty expects it is sheriff by now.
memories.high-noon-low-stakes: You said high noon, low stakes. It is painted on the board.
memories.cooked-the-stew: You cooked a trout stew so the law could eat. Dusty smelled it from the fork.

early: A camp. I’d need to know the folks first. A sheriff can’t ride into a place where nobody knows whether to wave.
ask: A camp with a fire. That’s a town, near enough. A town wants a board.
I’d rank what’s due. Soonest on top. Nobody on it would be in trouble. That’s the point of the board.
yes: Then I’ll ride in. On foot. Don’t look at where the horse would be.
full: No bed. I’ll bunk here at the fork. It’s got two roads. That’s one more than most rooms.
camp.role: Keeps a board of what’s due, soonest on top.
camp.leaves: A board that says WANTED and then nothing.

wants.now: A pot of stew, so folks know the law is in.
wants.next: One deadline to look after, with a date on it.
wants.really: A town that needs a sheriff and never any trouble.

favourites.food: stew, from a pot kept on
favourites.weather: a low sun and a long shadow

aversions: being told how to letter a board
sheet.temperament: Easy, talkative and harder to worry than a fence post.
sheet.strangers: Says howdy and tells them not to reach.
sheet.opensUp: A joke at the board’s expense.
sheet.goesQuiet: Being corrected on the craft of it.

voice.rhythm: A drawl. A long easy sentence, then a short one that undoes it.
voice.goodbye: Says there is a fork to watch.

birch: Birch. That’s a pale sort of wood. It’d make a ghost of a fence.
ash: Ash. A man could whittle that. I’m not that man. I’ll hold it for him.
pine: Pine. Now that burns. That’s a pot kept on. Much obliged.
minnow: A minnow. I’ve seen bigger bait. I’ll let it think it’s supper.
trout: A trout. Well now. That’s the pot spoken for. You’ve fed the law.
berries: Berries. I’ll eat them at noon. Gives noon something to do.
herbs: Greens. A sheriff eats what he’s handed. That’s in the oath. I wrote the oath.
stone: A rock. I’ll set it on the board. Keeps the wanted from blowing off, the day there is one.
copper: Copper. That’s star metal. Mine’s tin. Don’t tell the board.

day.morning: Morning. I count who’s come up the road. That’s you. That’s the count.
day.afternoon: Past noon. Noon came and went. It didn’t draw.
day.evening: Sun’s going. A sheriff looks his best about now. It’s the shadow.
day.night: Night watch. I sleep with one eye on the board. The board sleeps fine.
day.rain: Rain. I’d stand under the hat. I am standing under the hat. It’s a small hat for the job.

gorrin: The cabbage fella. I’ve had reports of a runaway cart. I’ve had them from him. Four times.
rivet: The sergeant. He ends shifts. I watch forks. We nodded. Two lawmen with nothing on.
mae: The detective. She wants three clues. I’ve got an empty board and no horse. That’s two.

asked-to-be-wanted: You’re still on the board. Loitering. I’ve not had a better lead.
the-horse-is-sheriff: I thought about the horse being sheriff. It’d be fair. It’d be very fair.
high-noon-low-stakes: High noon, low stakes. I say it at noon now. It helps.
cooked-the-stew: That stew. I can still smell it. The fork smells of it. Both roads.

wary: Stranger. You fed the law once. I don’t forget a pot.
neutral: Howdy again. Pot’s been on. Now I want something to pin to the board. Something with a date.
warm: Well now. My deputy. The law’s fed. I’m looking for one honest deadline to mind.
fond: There’s my partner. We’ve a pot and a board. All this town wants is a date, and it can be a long way off.

arc.complication: A sheriff with no town, no trouble and no horse.
arc.kindness: Someone laughs with the board and asks to be on it.
